product_desc: Written by Mark Manson, ed. Alpina, 320 pp. Never before in human history have we lived so well: conquered many diseases, gained access to the world's knowledge and surrounded ourselves with the comfort of technology. However, the better life becomes, the more we worry and worry. We live with the feeling that everything sucks. The planet is warming up, economic inequality is going through the roof, politicians are stealing and lying. Our uncertainty about the future, despair and hope that everything will be fine, are skillfully used by all and sundry - from marketers who impose another unnecessary service or product on us, to religious and political figures. What to do? Stop hoping for the best, says Mark Manson, world-bestselling author of The Subtle Art of Not Giving a Fuck. In his new book, he talks about a crisis of hope, about the futility of believing in a just world, and about how the quality of our lives is determined by the quality of our personality, and not by what blessings or hardships the world showers on us. Drawing on the wisdom of Nietzsche and Kant, Plato and Tom Waits, the author will help you develop a sober view of everything that surrounds you. After all, everywhere you look - everywhere is really bad. So it was and always will be. It's time to stop running from this truth and learn to accept life as it is.

With its dark purple color, black rice is a cultivated form of wild rice and has been around for more than 9,000 years. Eventually, it became available for everyone and came to this day as a grain that is synonymous with good health and long life.

Polenta, which refers to any hulled and crushed grain, is both a specific type of corn and a creamy northern Italian dish. It is more consistent in particle size than grits, and is generally milled to a fine or medium-coarse texture. It's made from flint corn, which has a hard, starchy endosperm that offers more texture than softer dent corn. Polenta is usually made with yellow corn, which is what gives this ingredient its golden hue. Serve it as a creamy base alongside braised short ribs, chili, or Parmesan Pork, or even in the form of French fries. In the grocery store, you'll find instant, quick-cooking, and traditional polenta; as the labels indicate, the first two are speedier and require less hands-on cooking because they're par-cooked, whereas traditional polenta offers the best texture and flavor, as the corn slowly releases its starches and sweetness in about 45 minutes.

Top 5 health benefits of prawns: A useful source of vitamins: Prawns are a useful source of the B group of vitamins, including B12 and folate. These vitamins play an important role in energy production and replenishing red blood cells. Prawns provide about 22 times the vitamin E levels of either chicken or beef. This fat-soluble vitamin acts as an antioxidant and may be protective against heart disease and cancer. A source of important trace minerals: Prawns are a useful source of some harder-to-get trace minerals, such as iodine, zinc and selenium. We need iodine to support the correct function of the thyroid gland, while zinc and selenium support the immune system. A source of protective antioxidants: Prawns have a pink hue thanks to a compound called astaxanthin, which is obtained through the algae that prawns eat. This compound has anti-inflammatory properties and may reduce the risk of some chronic diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, and be beneficial for skin health. May support weight loss: Shellfish such as prawns is an excellent source of easily digestible, high-quality protein. It's also low in calories and fat and may be a useful inclusion in a weight loss plan. Constitutes one of the recommended two portions of seafood per week: A healthy, balanced diet should include at least two portions of fish or seafood per week, and one portion should be an oily variety of fish. Shellfish, like prawns, constitutes one of these recommended portions. product_name: OCEAN FISH Cold Smoked Headless Mackerel, 300g
product_desc: Mackerels are considered some of the most nutritious fishes. They're an excellent source of protein, vitamins B2, B3, B6, and B12, and vitamin D. Their flesh is also full of minerals like copper, selenium, and iodine. Some of these fishes also contain good amounts of iron and vitamin B1. As mackerels belong to the "oily fish" category, they're one of the best sources of omega-3s — good fats that keep your heart and brain healthy. Another nutritional benefit of mackerels is that they have significantly higher amounts of good unsaturated fats than saturated fats — fats that increase your bad cholesterol. In fact, about 77% of the fat in mackerel is unsaturated. There are many well-known health benefits of mackerel. As a rich source of vitamins, minerals, and good fats, these are some of the ways eating this fish could benefit you: May boost heart health. The American Heart Association recommends eating at least two servings of fatty fish like mackerel per week. There's a reason for that. Mackerels, being oily fish, have high amounts of omega-3s. These good fats are known to reduce blood pressure and decrease the levels of cholesterol in your body. Studies have shown that those who eat mackerel regularly have lower blood pressure and less cholesterol in their blood. Having lower blood pressure means your heart doesn't have to work too hard to pump blood. Similarly, less cholesterol leads to less fat buildup in the arteries of your heart. As a result, your heart will stay strong and face fewer problems. Many prevent brain disorders. The omega-3s present in mackerel — particularly DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) — also play a big role in brain development. These fats control the release of chemical messengers in your brain, in turn helping to maintain brain function. Studies also show that consuming marine omega-3s — like those in mackerel — can reduce your risk of mental health issues like depression, bipolar disorder, and autism. May strengthen bones. There are many nutrients in mackerels that can help to keep your bones healthy. The most vital one is vitamin D. This vitamin helps in the metabolism of phosphorus and calcium — two minerals your bones need to grow. Getting enough vitamin D can lower your risk of bone loss and fracture. product_name: Paul Kalanithi. With my last breath
product_desc: Paul Kalanithi's astonishing volume of memoirs represents the emotional and lucid chronicle of the transformation of an idealistic and enthusiastic medical student into a successful neurosurgeon with an important career ahead, then into a patient and father who must face his own death. At the age of thirty-six, Paul Kalanithi discovered that he was suffering from lung cancer. It was the beginning of a radical change: the doctor who treats patients in the terminal phase turns into the patient who is fighting to live. Why is life worth living?

product_name: Friedman Tova, Brabant Malcolm. Daughter from Auschwitz
product_desc: Tova Friedman was a little girl from a large and happy Jewish family living in central Poland. She was able to survive Auschwitz (Auschwitz) and all its horrors, reunite with her family and not lose faith and hope. This book is the story of her life and overcoming trials.

product_name: Zulfa Katuh. How long do lemons bloom?
product_desc: Salama is an 18-year-old girl, a student at the Faculty of Pharmacy. She leads a peaceful and loving life with her family in Homs, Syria. When civil war breaks out, the world she knows is taken from her: her home, her loving family, her education, her economic stability, even her security. Her only close relative who remains alive is Laila, her pregnant sister-in-law, whom Salama wants to save. While searching for a safe way to emigrate, Salama meets a young protester with mysterious green eyes named Kenan, and it changes everything...

This book is for you if: - You are angry because you feel bad even when you should feel good; - You went through a divorce, through a toxic relationship, you were neglected as a child or abused; - You want to understand why you always feel mentally ill, exhausted, at the end of your patience; - You feel that you have many unhealed wounds and you don't know how to make peace with a painful past; - You feel ashamed and guilty and constantly tell yourself that you are a "weak man";

Colin Hoover is an author whom readers trust with their hearts. She is a global trend, a literary phenomenon of our time, a three-time winner of the Goodreads Choice Award in the Romance Novel category. A book about an eighteen-year-old girl with scars on her face (and more) who wants to become an actress. And about a guy my age who wants to be a writer. And then they met... spark, storm, madness. But the catch is that the next day she flies off to build a career. And they make an agreement: to meet every year, for one day, until the age of 23...

product_name: Isabelle Duvernois. Body language. Attention, gestures speak for us!
product_desc: Did you know that almost 70% of our communication takes place through non-verbal means: through gestures, walking, looking? With the help of this richly illustrated book, which contains many practical tips and testimonials, you will learn to decode all body gestures: blushing, crossing your arms or legs, posture of your torso, stroking your hair, your neck or your hand behind your back; all these gestures that our body makes, most often involuntarily, will no longer have secrets for you. 224 pages

Edward Fosca is a killer. Mariana Andros, a brilliant psychotherapist, has no doubt about this. Fosca, Professor of Greek Tragedy at Cambridge, is handsome and charismatic and adored by colleagues and students alike, especially members of a secret society known as the Virgins. Mariana becomes possessed by a group of Virgins when one of its members is found dead in Cambridge. A graduate of this university herself, Mariana suspects that behind the idyllic beauty of the bell towers and towers, behind the ancient traditions, something sinister is hidden...

product_name: Dale Carnegie. Secrets of success. Ed. Collection
product_desc: Donna Dale Carnegie continues the work of her father (who himself had a habit of revising his works), while being careful not to alter the spirit of the classic book. The volume preserves the structure, the renowned principles, the balance between theory and anecdotes, the engaging rhythm and the unmistakable philosophy of life. As many readers have noticed, the invitation to "influence" people in the original title is not about manipulation, but a way to win them over by smiling, being polite, sincere, and empathetic.

product_name: Michele Cushatt. The Healing Power of Faith
product_desc: Michele Cushatt has always used her voice to bring comfort to those in need. As a motivational speaker, preacher and radio personality, her words have been heard by hundreds of thousands of people around the world. That is precisely why the diagnosis of tongue cancer fell like a bolt of lightning on his family. But not for Michele, for she understood early on the healing power of faith and the fact that every trial in life is meant to test our devotion. If you are in a situation where sadness, grief, uncertainty, or shame is affecting your relationship with God, this book will help you discover the light at the end of the tunnel.

Roman Nicolae Dabija's novel is a model of the Romanian language. It is a sign that Bessarabia is also written well, and in some places - even better than in Bucharest or Galati. Bessarabians should not have complexes: the great Romanian literature is also written in Chisinau, like anywhere in the country where a master creates. If Romanians buy hundreds of copies of the same book, it means that we are witnessing a revolution in the field of books, which should make us happy.

The book by the writer Claudia Partole "Rebela, the bad of the good and the ugly of the beautiful" is the diary of a teenage girl and, as this kind of writing requires, it records confessions and reflections ordered chronologically. The driving force behind a 15-year-old girl's diary is rebellion. The frond gestures are, in general, age-specific, and in the given case the author follows the reactions of a minor, whose parents are divorcing. The prose "Rebela" will be able to be used from several perspectives, equally effectively by students, teachers and parents.

product_name: Chris Van Tulleken. Ultra processed people
product_desc: Do you know what you are eating? The truth about ultra-processed foods in our daily menus. Stabilizers, emulsifiers, gums, lecithin, glucose, hydrogenated oils. Ultra-processed foods are everywhere in our stores. We find them on shelves with sweets, dairy products, sauces, bread or even on shelves with organic products. Are they the solution to a nutritious and healthy diet?

product_name: Colleen Hoover. It all starts with us
product_desc: Before It all starts with us, the story started with Atlas. Lily and Ryle have finally found their balance in life and civilly share custody of their daughter, Emerson. Now, two years after their last talk, Lily meets Atlas by chance. He is overjoyed because it finally seems like the time is right for their feelings to blossom into a real relationship. Therefore, Atlas asks Lily out on a date. But Lily's joy turns to anxiety and terror. Although Ryle is no longer her husband, he is still a part of her life and would resent any man she chooses to date. He just hates the thought of Atlas Corrigan being a part of Lily and Emerson's life. Written from the perspective of Lily and Atlas, the novel It All Begins With Us gives readers a foray into Atlas' past as he and Lily rediscover their connection and rekindle the flame of their teenage love. At the same time, they have to deal with Lily's ex-husband. Ryle, an impulsive man, believes that Atlas is one of the reasons for the breakdown of his marriage.

product_name: Shafak Elif. The girl who didn't like her name
product_desc: The heroine of the story, Sakiz Sardunya, meaning Flowing Bitten, is unhappy with his name, and the naughty boys in the class laugh when they hear it. Sakiz is a good student, she loves nature and wants to start an environmental protection campaign at school, but she is afraid that such a campaign would be difficult to lead because of her name. And Sakiz has another passion: he loves the library, he likes to read. And it is this passion that makes her discover in a library an enchanted globe that gathers energy around the books and whose power decreases when it is away from the books. And this enchanted globe is left in the library by two children who need it to return to a miraculous world, on the eighth continent that has never known pollution and has no plastic bottles. Together with his new friends, Sakiz reaches, thanks to winged horses, the eighth continent, which however faces a problem: the plants are drying up there because people stopped dreaming, did not give free rein to their fantasy. And Sakiz finds the solution, he urges the children there to invent stories with the help of drawings and words. And nature revives!

product_name: Shh! Press the buttons and listen to the sounds!
product_desc: All the animals in the jungle are so noisy! Explore the jungle and find out why Daddy Lion asks everyone to keep quiet. Can you guess why he does it?

product_name: Stefanie Stahl. Healing of the inner child
product_desc: What would you say if you found out that, when two people are arguing, the conflict is not actually triggered by two adults with a solid self-awareness, but by the children inside each of them? Whether we have problems related to confidence in our own strength, we doubt that our partner, boss or new acquaintance really likes us or we often have difficulties in relating, the reason is that we associate ugly or even traumatic memories with childhood; or maybe some of us had an unhappy childhood, but repressed these experiences. Psychotherapist Stefanie Stahl is of the opinion that only when we get to know the child in us and become friends with him will we realize what resentments and deep wounds we have inside us. Then we will be able to accept this wounded part of our soul and heal it. Thus, confidence in ourselves will grow, and the child in us will finally find a refuge.

product_name: Haste, lazy! Press the buttons and listen to the sounds!
product_desc: The sloth is going home in his little car, but everyone around is in such a hurry! Accompany Leneș, as well as his friends, on their way home, at the end of which a wonderful surprise awaits you. Can you guess what it is?

product_desc: This is the children's first day at nursery school! But Jack is not pleased. The emotions we experience can do us a lot of harm, especially when we don't know how to fight them. To find out how Jack's first day at nursery ended, open this book. And as you read, you will learn how to control the emotions that Jack went through.

product_name: Viktor Frankl. Man in search of the meaning of life
product_desc: "Man in search of the meaning of life" is the chronicle of the terrible experiences experienced by the psychiatrist Viktor Frankl during his detention in Auschwitz and other concentration camps. The book, which has become an international bestseller with over 10 million copies sold, opens the most intimate perspective on the understanding of man in unsurvivable situations, how he accepts trauma and, in the end, finds meaning in what he lives.

product_name: Stefanie Stahl. Healing the inner child. Practical guide
product_desc: We all long to be accepted and loved. Ideally, during childhood we acquire self-confidence and positive beliefs that will help us develop harmoniously. But the negative experiences we live in childhood shape and unconsciously determine our entire approach to adult life.

Leadership is not a license to work less; it's a responsibility to work harder. And here's the problem: leadership is work. It means time and energy. Its effects are not easy to measure and are not always immediate. Leadership means being dedicated to people. Humanity has flourished for 50,000 years not because we are inclined to take care of ourselves, but because we are stimulated to take care of others. All that is needed is for the leaders to give us a good reason to put ourselves in the service of one another.

Unhappy marriages are often due to a simple reason, according to author Gary Chapman: we speak different love languages. In his experience of over 30 years as a marriage counselor, dr. Gary Chapman identified five love languages: words of encouragement, time spent with the loved one, gifts, services and physical contact. The book addresses each of them separately, in an accessible style, which is not without humor.

product_name: Ana Huang. Upside down games. It's at any cost
product_desc: Always confident, serious, taciturn and arrogant, the elite bodyguard RHYS LARSEN is guided by two rules in life: he protects his clients at all costs and does not get emotionally involved. Never! And he never felt tempted to break his rules…until he met her. Bridget von Ascheberg is a princess, literally, whose stubbornness rivals that of her bodyguard. A hidden flame burns within her, turning Rhys's rules to dust and powder. Bridget is not at all what he expected, but at the same time, she is just what Rhys needed.

product_name: Ana Huang. Perverted hatred. Enemies with advantages
product_desc: Gorgeous and arrogant, Josh Chen is preparing to become a doctor. So far, he hasn't met any girl who can resist him - with the exception of the damned Jules Ambrose. Ever since they met, the beautiful redhead has been like a thorn in his side, but at the same time, Jules obsesses him like no one else has. When the antipathy between them simply "explodes", resulting in a memorable night, Josh proposes a solution that - he hopes - will help him forget the obsession that grinds him: an "enemies with benefits" type arrangement, with simple rules. No jealousy. No strings attached. And it is absolutely impossible to fall in love with each other.

Charming, dangerous and smart enough to hide his intentions, CHRISTIAN HARPER is a monster who dresses like a true gentleman in tailored suits. He is completely unprincipled and has no need for love, but he cannot deny that he feels a strange attraction to the young woman who lives on the floor below him. She is the object of his darkest desires, the only mystery he cannot solve. When he gets the chance to get closer to her, Christian breaks his own rules and offers her an agreement that is hard to refuse. Every monster has a weakness. She is his weakness.

product_name: Leil Lowndes. How to communicate with anyone
product_desc: Have you ever admired those successful people who seemed to have everything? they speak confidently at parties, they speak knowledgeably in business meetings, they have the best jobs, they throw the most beautiful parties and have the most interesting friends. but that doesn't necessarily mean they're smarter than you or better looking. it's just how they communicate with others. With 92 effective, easy-to-understand techniques from Leil Lowndes, you'll learn how to become a master communicator in life, love, and business. Combining the latest specialized research with the author's observations about people's weaknesses, this book will show you: • how to make a memorable entrance and talk to people you've always wanted to meet; • how to use body language to captivate the audience; • how to appear like oneself in a crowd of strangers, despite how little you have in common; • how to always appear confident and charismatic, no matter where you are.

product_name: Colleen Hoover. It used to be perfect
product_desc: Is it possible for a love story with a perfect beginning to survive a lifetime, between two imperfect people? Quinn never suspected that she would meet her great love, Graham, at her fiance's door. A year later, we find the two in a perfect relationship, as if predestined for each other, after both broke up with their partners, who were cheating on them... with each other. Seven years later, their love - once perfect - is in danger of being destroyed.

One of the most impressive love stories An impressive love story in the spirit of the interwar period, created by Mikhail Drumesh, has stood the test of time and has become one of the author's most valuable works. Anda and Dinu, two young people who seem destined for each other, experience suspenseful adventures and exciting twists and turns, all in the name of perfect love. But life, with its harsh inexorability, will test them and disturb their dreams. This Story is as old as the world: from love to war there is only one step.”

product_name: Eva Mozes Kor, Lisa Rojany Buccieri. Twins from Auschwitz
product_desc: In the summer of 1944, Eva Mozes Kor and her family arrived at Auschwitz. Here all its members were separated: the two older sisters and the parents were taken directly to the gas chambers, while Eva and her twin sister, Miriam, were handed over to Dr. Josef Mengele, who became known as the "Angel of Death." At that time, the two girls were only ten years old.

product_name: Mihail Drumes. Invitation to a waltz
product_desc: An all-consuming and self-destructive love story The Waltz Invitation is one of the most appreciated novels of interwar literature, and in the almost ninety years that have passed since its first appearance, in 1936, it has been published in dozens of editions. Drumeș tells the love story between Tudor and Micaela, an experience ground by emotional excesses, jealousy and games of seduction. A love story or a revenge story? And one, and another, the Waltz Invitation gives the rhythm of a dizzying dance - and by no means a simple waltz -, which will leave you breathless.

One of the best-selling Romanian literature books of all time First published in 1946, Dima the Seventh Grader has never lost its charm. The love story between Grig and Lotte, the adventurous spirit, idealism, impertinence, naivety and enthusiasm of the young people in Drumeș's novel remain as current. Like all teenagers, Dima, Tarzan, Magotu, Basu and all the others dream and live everything to the fullest. Plans for a spectacular expedition, conflicts with teachers, inner dramas, passionate loves, all these are captured and described by Mihail Drumeș with naturalness and talent, fascinating generations of readers.

Almost everyone in the village is a suspect, including the most respected people. Miss Marple, an observant and wise old woman, uses her signature method - analyzing everyday behavior and little things that no one notices - to solve the crime. What makes this book special: - This isn't just a detective story, but a true portrait of English village life, with its ironic characters, rumors, and hidden passions.
